The scale parameter

Every block in this project takes a scale parameter. We set it once in the main program — then all shapes resize together automatically.

Why scale?

Without scale, every shape is a fixed size — if you want to make the house bigger you’d have to edit every single block. With scale, you change one number in the main program and the whole house resizes.

// the_door uses scale × 3 (width) and scale × 5 (height)
scale = 1  →  door width = 1 × 3 = 3 steps,  door height = 1 × 5 = 5 steps
scale = 2  →  door width = 2 × 3 = 6 steps,  door height = 2 × 5 = 10 steps
scale = 5  →  door width = 5 × 3 = 15 steps, door height = 5 × 5 = 25 steps
scale = 10 →  door width = 10 × 3 = 30 steps, door height = 10 × 5 = 50 steps
← this is the actual Scratch block inside the_door — scale * 3 means the width changes every time you change scale

We define scale once in the main program (when 🚩 clicked) and pass it into every block call. Click any card above to see how each block uses it.

Each block — pseudocode + animation

Every shape is drawn with REPEAT 2: move → turn 90° → move → turn 90°, repeated twice. Only the numbers change. The scale parameter is set in the main program — explained at the end.

Scratch blocks

DEFINE the_roof(scale): point in direction 45° ← 45° = up-right diagonal move scale × 13 steps ← up to peak point in direction 135° ← 135° = down-right diagonal move scale × 13 steps ← down to right corner point in direction -90° ← face left (-90 = 180, same thing) move scale × 18 steps ← back home along base point in direction 90° ← reset direction
Why height = 9?

The roof base is 18. Half of 18 = 9. When height = half the base, both sides of the triangle make a perfect 45° angle.

half-base = 9, height = 9
tan(angle) = 9 ÷ 9 = 1 → angle = 45° ✓
diagonal = √(9² + 9²) = 9√2 ≈ 12.73 → 13 steps

45° is the cleanest angle in Scratch — no awkward decimals, easy to explain, and the two slopes are perfectly symmetric.

Animation

What is scale?

scale is a parameter — a number we pass in when we call the block. It controls how big the shape is drawn. We set the actual value in the main program (when 🚩 clicked). That way all shapes scale together automatically.

Step 1 — Plan it on paper first 📝
✏️ Always plan before coding! This hand-drawn sketch shows why each pen-up movement uses those exact x and y values. Understanding the plan = understanding the code.
What the plan tells us 🗺️
🖊️ Movement ≠ Drawing! The x/y movements just position the pen at the right starting point. The actual drawing is done by calling the block we built on Tab 2. Think of it as: walk to the spot, then draw the shape.
① 1st point
call the_roof scale — draws the roof from the starting point. No movement needed, this is where we begin.
→ 2nd point
Pen up → change x by scale×2 → pen down
Move right 2 units to reach the wall's start corner
② 2nd point
call the_wall scale — draws the wall rectangle. The block does all the drawing!
→ 3rd point
Pen up → change y by scale×−2 then change x by scale×3 → pen down
Move down 2, right 3 to reach window_1's top-left corner
③ 3rd point
call window_1 scale — draws the 3×3 square window.
→ 4th point
Pen up → change x by scale×5 then change y by scale×−4 → pen down
Move right 5, down 4 to reach the door's top-left corner
④ 4th point
call the_door scale — draws the 3×5 door rectangle.
→ last point
Pen up → change x by scale×−7 then change y by scale×−1 → pen down
Move left 7, down 1 to reach window_2's top-left corner
⑤ last point
call window_2 scale — draws the 2×2 small square window.
💡 Count the grid squares!
Every x/y number comes directly from counting squares in the sketch — the dimensions of the shapes tell you how far to move.
Step 2 — This is YOUR hierarchy 🗂️
🗂️ This is YOUR hierarchy  draw_the_house decides the order the parts are drawn. There is no single correct order — you are the designer. You could draw the windows before the door, biggest shape first, or smallest first. This is your creative decision!

You can reorder however you want:

Your order ✓
  1. the_roof
  2. the_wall
  3. window_1
  4. the_door
  5. window_2
Could also be…
  1. the_wall
  2. the_roof
  3. window_2 (small → big)
  4. window_1
  5. the_door

As long as your pen up → move → pen down positions are correct for the order you choose, it works!

Step 3 — Your Scratch blocks

Now that the plan is clear, here is the actual Scratch code. Every x/y number matches exactly what you drew on paper.

💡 draw_the_house is the boss block — it calls all 5 custom blocks in order and handles all the pen up/down movements between them. Change the order here and you change the drawing sequence!

The complete Scratch project
🎉 All blocks together  Here is the full Scratch code — every custom block you built, plus the main script that calls them all.
Why draw_the_house 10?

The 10 is the scale — it flows into every single block call:

draw_the_house(10) → the_roof(10) move 10 × 13 = 130 steps diagonal → the_wall(10) move 10 × 14 = 140 steps wide move 10 × 11 = 110 steps tall → window_1(10) move 10 × 3 = 30 steps each side → the_door(10) move 10 × 3 = 30 steps wide move 10 × 5 = 50 steps tall → window_2(10) move 10 × 2 = 20 steps each side

✨ Change the 10 → the whole house resizes!
